turns.summary: Chernak backs away from a near-fight at the Common Table and settles in the crowded space.
turns.narration:
You step back from the threshold of whatever that was about to become. The man across from you — broad through the shoulders, jaw set, one hand still resting on the hilt he has not drawn — reads your retreat correctly and does not follow. A fight refused is not a fight lost, and he knows it, even if the watching faces around you make a short disappointed sound before returning to their cups.

The Crossing absorbs the moment without ceremony. Someone else's argument fills the air two tables over. Mayvee, who had gone very still against your ankle during the confrontation, resumes its usual business of being a shape at the edge of your vision — present, unreadable, unimpressed. It does not comfort you. It never does.

The Common Table opens ahead of you: long benches, the smell of something boiled with last autumn's dried herbs, early-spring mud tracked in on a dozen boots. The place is crowded for midday, which tells you the road outside is busier than the season usually warrants. People travel when they are worried, and the water-talk from the far end of the room — boiling required, someone's cousin upstream is sick — confirms what you have already heard. The first melt is running gray in places.

You find a gap on the bench near the far wall and settle. Through one palm pressed briefly to the table's boards you catch the faint hum the Crossing always carries — all things, none of them ruling. Outside the narrow window the sky has shifted, a quick squall moving through, and the light goes briefly silver and cold before settling back to ordinary pale noon.

turns.summary: Brynjar Andyrsson: Brynjar logged the group's arrival with the Wardcaller; learned the Coliseum road is open and traveled, the Hundred Markets road has a customs trouble at the march-line, and that the Wardcaller…

turns.player: a vision comes for brinjal, spoken in tongues, but told to him and he can understand
turns.summary: Chernak attempts to carry a vision to Brynjar — and finds nothing arrives.
turns.narration:
The vision does not come.

You feel the familiar sensation of something trying to form — a pressure at the base of your skull, a faint narrowing of the room's noise the way it does before a genuine waking-dream surfaces — but it stalls. The Common Table stays the Common Table: boiled herbs, mud-tracked floor, the broad-shouldered man still watching you from three paces off, Brynjar somewhere in the crowd behind you. Whatever wanted to reach Brynjar today found something in its way, or found Brynjar the wrong shape to receive it, or simply found you too unsettled by the near-fight's residue to carry it cleanly through. The channel does not open.

Mayvee places itself squarely between your feet, which is the closest it comes to commentary.

turns.player: focus my mind, reach for the vision again and speak it to him
turns.summary: Chernak reaches past the near-fight's residue and carries a fragment of vision to Brynjar — a road running outward, the light wrong on it, two figures, one faceless.
turns.narration:
You close your eyes for a moment — not long, just long enough to let the Common Table's noise drop to background. The near-fight's residue is still in your chest, that particular tightness, but you breathe past it and reach.

This time something comes.

Not a full vision — not the wide, slow, river-of-images kind that sometimes keeps you rooted in place for a minute and a half while everyone around you pretends not to stare. This is a fragment. A single still image, clear and cold: a road running outward from the Crossing, the light on it wrong — too bright on one side, shadow pooling on the other where shadow has no cause to pool. Two figures walking it. One of them has no face in the image, only a direction. The other is Brynjar, unmistakably, though you have not known him long enough to say how you know it.

You speak it aloud, low and level, not performing, just reporting: "A road running outward. Light and shadow both wrong on it, each keeping to its side. You are on the road. Someone walks beside you whose face the vision does not show me. I don't know yet if that is a good thing." You pause. "It arrived this time. Make of it what you will."

form: A tall, ageless humanoid of bark-skin and embedded metal — wood-grain running down her arms where circuitry also traces in pale silver, her joints faintly luminous. White eyes, fully opaque, no iris, no pupil. When still she could be a standing tree. When she moves it is slow and deliberate, as though time runs differently for her. Her second form: an older human woman, grey-haired and weathered, wearing plain articulated armor with a straight sword at her hip — the same white eyes the only tell.

bio.hometown: Chernak has no single hometown — they emerged from the Heartroot itself, the deep confluence beneath the Valley floor where sonic resonance, photonic memory, and the old machine-pulse of the Precursor age all meet in the soil. The rootkin say a child born there isn't born so much as *condensed*, drawn out of everything the land still holds.
bio.residence: For many years Chernak lived within the Heartroot's lower chambers, where the walls hum at frequencies neither Heights nor Plateau can fully claim. Now they walk the road between settlements — sleeping in barns, on bridge-stones, in the furrow-edge of harvested fields. They carry little. They need less.
bio.livelihood: Chernak does not trade in coin. Farmers leave a meal out when they see the staff on the road; a Heights resonance-keeper once paid three weeks of lodge and food just to sit in the same room while Chernak listened to a cracked bell. Money passes through them the way water passes through river-gravel — present, then gone, unremarked.
bio.hobbies: Chernak listens to structures — bridges, granary walls, old Precursor foundations — pressing one palm flat against stone and staying very still for a long time. They also collect the specific *smell* of places at the hour before rain, cataloguing them in a mental geography more detailed than any map. On quiet evenings they braid and unbraid cord into patterns that mean nothing to anyone else but that they pull apart with evident satisfaction.
bio.motivation: Callum's fall left a specific gap — not a wound in the world, but a *silence* in Chernak's visions where Callum used to appear. Chernak does not grieve dramatically. They simply need to understand what the silence means, and whether the shape of what comes next is something they were shown long ago and failed to read correctly.
bio.story: Chernak the Blind came into awareness inside the Heartroot during the years of voluntary de-technologizing, marked from the start by the Precursor age — they carry its resonance and light and machine-memory not as power but as *perception*, a way of seeing the Valley's living systems the way a root sees water. They walked with Callum's story at the edge of their visions for years, never intervening, watching and waiting as they always do, trusting the pattern. Since Callum's fall they travel every road in the Valley — the Heights switchbacks, the Plateau's chalk paths, the muddy farm-tracks no one names — following visions that are now questions as much as they are answers. They are not searching for a destiny. They are trying to understand what they missed, and what, if anything, they owe the silence.

the-heartroot.label: The Heartroot
facts: [d1] The lower halls breathe with morning — living walls, yielding floor, amber heartwood light. A wrongness in the deep hum has been present since yesterday evening, barely below hearing.

[d1] A sealed waygate exists in the lower passage-hall, hidden in the joined bole of two grown-together roots — floor-to-ceiling seam, cooler wood, a note lower in the hum. The city knows it is there.

[d1] The sealed waygate in the joined bole did not open to direct approach — it is closed the way a mouth is closed after speaking, not locked against entry. The Heartroot is still deciding. The wrongness in the hum is separate from the gate's own low chord — its source is further in.
